Menopause Is Not the End — It's a New Chapter
Menopause is a natural biological transition, yet for many women, it arrives accompanied by confusion, discomfort, and a concerning lack of reliable medical guidance. At Dr. Tanushree Pandey's clinic in South Mumbai, we believe every woman deserves clear information and supportive care through every stage of her reproductive life — including and beyond menopause.

Menopause is confirmed after 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period, typically between ages 45 and 55. The years leading up to it — perimenopause — can begin as early as the mid-30s, bringing with them a range of symptoms that are often attributed to stress, ageing, or other causes.

Common symptoms of perimenopause and menopause:
• Hot flashes and night sweats
• Irregular or heavy periods (in perimenopause)
• Sleep disturbances
• Mood changes, anxiety, or low mood
• Vaginal dryness and discomfort during intercourse
• Reduced libido
• Urinary frequency or leakage
• Cognitive changes, including difficulty concentrating
• Bone density loss (increasing risk of osteoporosis)

These symptoms are real, and they are treatable. Options range from lifestyle modifications and non-hormonal therapies to Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT), which — when appropriately prescribed — is safe and highly effective for most women.
At Dr. Pandey's clinic, menopause care is individualised, evidence-based, and delivered with the sensitivity this important life stage deserves.

Cervical Cancer Awareness: Prevention Saves Lives
Cervical cancer is one of the most preventable cancers — and yet it remains the second most common cancer among women in India. The reason this statistic persists is not lack of treatment; it is lack of awareness and access to screening.

Cervical cancer is caused almost entirely by persistent infection with high-risk strains of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) — a common virus transmitted through sexual contact. Critically, HPV infection often causes no symptoms at all, which is why regular screening is so essential.

What every woman should know:

PAP Smear: A cervical screening test that detects abnormal cells before they become cancerous. Recommended every 3 years from age 21, or every 5 years with combined HPV testing from age 30.

HPV Vaccination: Highly effective vaccines are available that protect against the most common cancer-causing HPV strains. Ideally given before sexual debut, but beneficial up to age 45 in many cases. Vaccination + screening together provide the strongest protection.

Warning signs to never ignore: unusual vaginal discharge (watery, foul-smelling, or blood-tinged), bleeding between periods or after intercourse, pelvic pain, and pain during intercourse.

When detected early, cervical cancer is highly treatable. When detected late, outcomes are significantly poorer. The difference, in most cases, is a simple, painless screening test.

Endometriosis: The Condition That Takes Too Long to Diagnose
Endometriosis affects approximately 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide — yet on average, it takes 7 to 10 years to receive a correct diagnosis. This delay is not just frustrating — it allows the condition to progress, causing increasing pain, damage to reproductive organs, and reduced fertility potential.

So what is endometriosis? It is a condition in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus — on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, bladder, bowel, and other surrounding structures. Each month, this tissue responds to hormonal changes just as the uterine lining does — swelling, breaking down, and bleeding — but with nowhere to go. This causes inflammation, the formation of scar tissue (adhesions), and often, intense pain.

Key symptoms to watch for:
• Severe menstrual cramps that worsen over time
• Chronic pelvic pain, not just during periods
• Pain during or after sexual intercourse
• Painful bowel movements or urination, especially during menstruation
• Heavy or irregular periods
• Difficulty conceiving

Endometriosis is frequently dismissed as "bad periods" — both by women themselves and sometimes by healthcare providers. If you have experienced any of these symptoms for more than a few cycles, a thorough gynaecological assessment is essential.

A Heartfelt Thank You to Dr. Asavari and Tulsi Gynaecologist Clinic

I cannot thank Dr. Asavari and her team at Tulsi Gynaecologist Clinic enough for the incredible care and support I received during both of my pregnancies.

Back in 2021, during my first pregnancy, I contracted COVID and was hospitalized for a week. It was an extremely difficult and scary time, but thanks to Dr. Asavari’s constant monitoring and support, I felt reassured and safe. Despite the complications, she kept a close weekly check on my baby's well-being, ensuring everything was progressing smoothly. Her calm guidance and expertise gave me the strength and clarity I needed throughout that challenging journey and I was blessed with a beautiful daughter who is now 3.10 years old. ❤️🙏

Now, 3.3 years later, I conceived again—this time while living in a different city. When I learned that my second pregnancy was going to be even more complicated, the first and only name that came to mind was Dr. Asavari. To my surprise and relief, she remembered me and, without hesitation, started guiding me through this new journey as well—even from afar. Despite the distance, she responded to all my queries with care, offering advice and reassurance at every stage.

Her dedication, compassion, and genuine concern for her patients' well-being are truly exceptional. I feel incredibly fortunate to have had her by my side during two of the most important journeys of my life.

Thank you, Dr. Asavari, for being more than just a doctor—you've been a guiding light, a strong support system, and a true blessing🤗🙏❤️
